extraction.name: DocVQA
extraction.description: A dataset for Visual Question Answering on document images consisting of 50,000 questions over 12,000+ document images.
extraction.creator: Minesh Mathew; Dimosthenis Karatzas; C.V. Jawahar
extraction.citeAs: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar. DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Document images were downloaded from the UCSF Industry Documents Library, pages were hand picked, and questions and answers were collected from remote workers in a three-stage annotation process including creation, verification, and author review.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Document images sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors minimized binarized images due to poor image quality and prioritized pages with tables, forms, lists and figures over pages with only running text.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation was done in three stages: workers created up to 10 question-answer pairs per image, a second worker verified answers and assigned question types while flagging ambiguous questions, and authors reviewed mismatches in a third stage.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Questions were verified by a second worker, assigned one or more question types, ambiguous or inapt questions could be flagged and excluded, and mismatched answers were reviewed and edited by the authors.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Up to 2 worker answer annotations per question, with a third-stage author review for disagreements
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to inspire a purpose-driven approach in document image analysis and support practical intelligent reading systems that respond to ad-hoc human information requests.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset favors non-binarized images and includes many documents from food and nutrition related collections because they had more non-binarized images.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Poor image quality from binarized documents was a concern, and current models perform much worse than humans, especially on questions requiring document structure understanding.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing of Visual Question Answering methods on document images, with baseline evaluation of VQA and reading comprehension models.

name.evidence: We present a new dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images called DocVQA.

description.evidence: We present a new dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images called DocVQA. The dataset consists of 50,000 questions defined on 12,000+ document images.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We downloaded documents from different collections and hand picked pages from these documents for use in the dataset. Questions and answers on the selected document images are collected with the help of remote workers, using a Web based annotation tool. The annotation process was organized in three stages.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: Images in the dataset are sourced from documents in UCSF Industry Documents Library1. We downloaded documents from different collections and hand picked pages from these documents for use in the dataset.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Document Images: Images in the dataset are sourced from documents in UCSF Industry Documents Library1.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: The final set of images in the dataset are drawn from pages of 6;071industry documents. We made use of documents from as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Majority of documents in the library are binarized and the binarization has taken on a toll on the image quality. We tried to minimize binarized images in DocVQA since we did not want poor image quality to be a bottleneck for VQA. We also prioritized pages with tables, forms, lists and figures over pages which only have running text.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: The annotation process was organized in three stages. In stage 1, workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs on it. The second annotation stage aims to verify the data collected in the first stage. Here a worker was shown an image and questions defined on it in the first stage (but not the answers from the first stage), and was required to enter answers for the questions. In this stage workers were also required to assign one or more question types to each question. If none of the answers entered in the first stage match exactly with any of the answers from the second stage, the particular question is sent for review in a third stage. Here questions and answers are editable and the reviewer either accepts the question-answer (after editing if necessary) or ignores it. The third stage review is done by the authors themselves.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: Questions and answers on the selected document images are collected with the help of remote workers, using a Web based annotation tool.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: The second annotation stage aims to verify the data collected in the first stage. In this stage workers were also required to assign one or more question types to each question. During the second stage, if the worker finds a question inapt owing to language issues or ambiguity, an option to flag the question was provided. Such questions are not included in the dataset. If none of the answers entered in the first stage match exactly with any of the answers from the second stage, the particular question is sent for review in a third stage.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: In stage 1, workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs on it. The second annotation stage aims to verify the data collected in the first stage. Here a worker was shown an image and questions defined on it in the first stage (but not the answers from the first stage), and was required to enter answers for the questions. If none of the answers entered in the first stage match exactly with any of the answers from the second stage, the particular question is sent for review in a third stage.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: By doing so, we seek to inspire a “purpose-driven” point of view in DAR research. In case of Document VQA, as illustrated in Figure 1, an intelligent reading system is expected to respond to ad-hoc requests for information, expressed in natural language questions by human users.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: We tried to minimize binarized images in DocVQA since we did not want poor image quality to be a bottleneck for VQA. We use many documents from food and nutrition related collections, as they have a good number of non-binarized images.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Majority of documents in the library are binarized and the binarization has taken on a toll on the image quality. We tried to minimize binarized images in DocVQA since we did not want poor image quality to be a bottleneck for VQA. Although the existing models perform reasonably well on certain types of questions, there is large performance gap compared to human performance (94.36% accuracy). The models need to improve specifically on questions where understanding structure of the document is crucial.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The data is split randomly in an 80�10�10 ratio to train, validation and test splits. We define and evaluate various baseline methods over the DocVQA dataset, ranging from simple heuristic methods and human performance analysis that allow us to define upper performance bounds given different assumptions, to state of the art Scene Text VQA models and NLP models.
